nodes.label: AMPM Technical Architecture and Integration Plan (DRAFT v0.2)
Technology decisions register (T-1 to T-14)
nodes.rationale: This document recommends; AMPM decides. Every recommendation that depends on an open question carries a T-n decision ID naming the question, the alternative and the cost of changing later.

nodes.label: T-1 Platform form factor: native iOS and Android apps plus static web
nodes.rationale: Originally one responsive TypeScript web platform with PWA offline in Phase 4; AMPM changed to native team and client apps from one React Native (Expo) codebase, offline-first, with the public website on Next.js. Front-end effort roughly doubles; the backend is unchanged.

nodes.label: T-2 AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1) with Hyderabad backup copies
nodes.rationale: All personal data stays in India; containers and PostgreSQL keep the platform portable to Google Cloud or Azure India regions. Still open with AMPM.

nodes.label: T-3 Payment gateway adapter (Razorpay proposed; card and UPI required)
nodes.rationale: Hosted checkout and webhook-driven activation; offline payments recorded manually activate the same way. AMPM selects the provider; PayU, Cashfree or Stripe India fit the same adapter.

nodes.label: T-4 WhatsApp, Amazon SES and DLT-registered SMS behind one adapter
nodes.rationale: Any provider swap is an adapter change; dropping WhatsApp removes the longest onboarding lead time.

nodes.label: T-5 Built-in content tables (dropped)
nodes.rationale: AMPM decided there is no content editor; the website is static and maintained outside the app, so the cms_* tables are not built.

nodes.label: T-6 Authentication inside the API
nodes.rationale: Argon2id passwords, authenticator codes for staff, server-side sessions in secure cookies, guest access by tokenised link, no self-registration anywhere. Changed: OTP sign-in for clients and prospects; staff method to be finalised.

nodes.label: T-7 Sizing: modular monolith for about 200 hotels and 20 concurrent weddings
nodes.rationale: One API and one worker serve this with room for tenfold growth by adding replicas; module boundaries are the seams for a later split.

nodes.label: T-8 INR, English, Asia/Kolkata, GST fields optional
T-9 Data protection: consent, retention proposals, DPDP 2023
nodes.rationale: Changed: no automatic deletion; retention actions require AMPM approval.

nodes.label: T-10 Full production topology from Phase 1
nodes.rationale: No throwaway hosting; a reduced Phase 1 could run single-AZ on the same code.

nodes.label: T-11 Offline-first behaviour with sync and conflict log
nodes.rationale: Originally Phase 4 service-worker caching; changed to offline-first native apps from launch with sync, conflict detection and protected local storage.

nodes.label: T-12 Proposed service-level targets
nodes.rationale: 99.5 percent monthly availability, API p95 under 400 ms, pages interactive under 3 s on 4G, WCAG 2.1 AA; still open.

nodes.label: T-13 Backups: 35-day PITR, cross-region copies, RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h
nodes.rationale: Tighter targets need a warm standby in the second region at roughly double the database cost.

nodes.label: T-14 On-call cover on wedding days and deployment freeze while live
Architecture changes from AMPM decisions of 25 October 2026
Architecture principles (§1)
nodes.rationale: Derived from the specification rather than invented; each principle names its source.

nodes.label: Principle: one backend, several experiences
nodes.rationale: One API and one database serve website, client portal, team workspace and guest portal (SPEC §10); nothing is copied between experiences.

nodes.label: Principle: authorisation lives in the API and storage layer
nodes.rationale: Never only in the interface (SPEC §6.1); files reachable only through short-lived signed links; exports run through the same filters.

nodes.label: Principle: modular monolith, not microservices
nodes.rationale: At T-7 scale one deployable API and one worker are simpler, cheaper and easier for a small team; module boundaries follow the data model so a later split is a deployment change, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Principle: commercial rules are configuration
nodes.rationale: Plans, packages, categories, thresholds, templates and labels are database rows editable by the Super Admin (SPEC §10 avoid hard-coded commercial rules).

nodes.label: Principle: everything important is versioned, audited and recoverable
nodes.rationale: Soft deletes, immutable shared versions, append-only audit events, point-in-time recovery.

nodes.label: Principle: privacy by design
nodes.rationale: Field visibility classes, a separate restricted bucket for identity documents, minimal guest data, retention jobs, consent captured where data enters (BIZ rule 7, SPEC §2.5).

nodes.label: Principle: managed, boring infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Managed PostgreSQL, object storage, queues and containers; infrastructure as code; nothing hand-built on a server.

nodes.label: Principle: integrations behind adapters
nodes.rationale: Payment, messaging, email, video and maps are each one interface with one provider implementation so a provider change never touches business logic.

nodes.label: System context (§2)
api container: NestJS modular monolith (REST, OpenAPI, WebSocket)
nodes.rationale: The only process that reads or writes the database and object storage on behalf of users; hosts the policy pipeline and the per-class serialisers.

nodes.label: worker container: BullMQ consumers, schedulers, webhooks
nodes.rationale: Same repository as the API, deployed separately so job load never slows requests; receives provider webhooks and shares the policy modules.

nodes.label: web-public container: Next.js static pages and guest RSVP portal
nodes.rationale: Separate from the authenticated app so guests and visitors never reach staff or client code paths; cached at the CDN.

nodes.label: web-app container: Next.js client portal, demo mode and team workspace
nodes.rationale: Server components fetch through the API with the session cookie; no direct database access from the web tier.

nodes.label: Team app: React Native iOS and Android, offline-first, department-scoped
Client app: React Native iOS and Android (web build open)
PostgreSQL 16 on RDS Multi-AZ with PITR
nodes.rationale: System of record, full-text hotel search, partitioned audit and notification tables; encrypted with a customer-managed key; read replica for reports when needed.

nodes.label: Redis (ElastiCache): queues, sessions, rate limits, caches, chat bus
nodes.rationale: Nothing in Redis is the only copy of anything.

nodes.label: Object storage: three S3 buckets by sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Media served via CDN signed URLs, documents via API-signed URLs, restricted identity documents with a separate key and no CDN; versioning and cross-region replication.

nodes.label: S3 restricted identity bucket (separate KMS key, no CDN, access audited)
Edge: CloudFront CDN with signed URLs, WAF, load balancer with TLS termination
Video delivery: Cloudflare Stream or Mux with signed playback
nodes.rationale: Controlled video delivery (SPEC §10) without building a transcoding pipeline; predictable cost per minute.

nodes.label: Technology choices as short ADRs (§4)
nodes.rationale: Each row names alternatives considered, why this one, reversibility after Phase 1 and the decision it is tied to.

nodes.label: TypeScript on Node 20 LTS end to end
nodes.rationale: One language across web and API; static types make the per-class serialisers checkable at compile time; large talent pool in India.

nodes.label: Next.js 14 (App Router)
nodes.rationale: Static generation for the marketing site, server rendering for portals, image optimisation.

nodes.label: NestJS API framework
nodes.rationale: Enforced module boundaries, dependency injection, guards and interceptors that map onto the policy pipeline, OpenAPI generation, separate deployable from the web tier.

nodes.label: Prisma ORM and migrations
nodes.rationale: Schema as code mirroring data-model.md; row scoping in a repository layer; PostgreSQL row-level security kept as optional hardening.

nodes.label: BullMQ on Redis for jobs and queues
nodes.rationale: Delayed and repeatable jobs, retries with backoff, per-queue concurrency, a dashboard; pg-boss is the simpler alternative if AMPM wants to avoid Redis.

nodes.label: React Native (Expo) native apps in TypeScript
nodes.rationale: One codebase for the team app and the client app sharing the API and the policy module; React Native Web could provide a client web build.

nodes.label: ECS Fargate compute behind an application load balancer and WAF
nodes.rationale: Managed containers without cluster operations; scales per service; fits a small team.

nodes.label: Terraform infrastructure as code with GitHub Actions CI and CD
nodes.rationale: Reproducible environments, reviewable infrastructure changes, no manual console work; trunk-based development.

nodes.label: Observability: CloudWatch logs, metrics and alarms; Sentry errors and traces
nodes.rationale: Enough signal for the scale; business audit stays in audit_events, not in logs.

nodes.label: AWS Secrets Manager and three customer-managed KMS keys
nodes.rationale: Keys for database, general storage and the restricted bucket give a separate blast radius for identity documents.

nodes.label: sharp image processing in the worker
nodes.rationale: Removes location metadata from guest-uploaded images; generates sizes once at upload.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL full-text and trigram hotel search
nodes.rationale: A few hundred hotels do not justify a search cluster; the search view is rebuilt by the worker when hotel data changes.

nodes.label: Workbox service worker offline caches (original Phase 4 plan)
nodes.rationale: Event-day resilience without an app store; superseded by native offline-first apps.

nodes.label: Testing: Vitest, Playwright, adapter contract tests, generated authorisation suite
nodes.rationale: The SPEC §12 tampering scenarios become automated tests.

nodes.label: Google Maps Platform (Street View Static and Maps SDK)
Real-time chat channel: Socket.IO on the API with a Redis message bus
nodes.rationale: Added for Q20 live chat; backed by the conversations and messages tables; push notifications wake the apps; a staff chat console lives in the team app.

nodes.label: Module boundaries inside the API (§5)
nodes.rationale: Modules mirror data-model.md; dependencies point downward only, which keeps the monolith modular and makes a later split possible.

nodes.label: Module rules enforced in code review
nodes.rationale: A module exposes a service interface and domain events; others never query its tables directly; cross-module reactions go through domain events handled by the worker; the shared kernel knows nothing about weddings; each module owns its Prisma models under one schema.

Policy pipeline: eight-step enforcement of the permission matrix (§6)
nodes.rationale: Authenticate, principal, entitlements, guard, repository scoping, service rule check, serialiser by class set, audit; every request, file download and export runs the same pipeline.

nodes.label: Server-side sessions in Redis with secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies
nodes.rationale: 12 hours idle for staff, 30 days for clients, revoked on role or membership change; guest tokens are exchanged once for a short session bound to the family group.

nodes.label: Repository-layer scoping by membership, is_demo, visibility and soft delete
nodes.rationale: Scoping lives in the repository rather than each service; PostgreSQL row-level security can be enabled in Phase 5 as a second line of defence.

nodes.label: Serialisers per visibility class (BudgetLineClientView, InternalView, FinanceView)
nodes.rationale: Fields outside the chosen model do not exist in the response, so hiding in the interface cannot happen by accident.

nodes.label: Denial equals absence: 404 for unseen records
Signed document download via document_access_links (15-minute URLs)
nodes.rationale: The API checks the owning record, mints a document_access_links row and returns a signed URL; identity-document reads also write an audit event and alert; otherwise 404.

nodes.label: Export pipeline in the worker with class stripping and audit
nodes.rationale: Exports run through the same guard and serialiser, then strip SENSITIVE, IDENTITY, BANK and SECRET classes regardless of role (P-10), and write an audit event with filters and row count.

nodes.label: Authorisation test suite generated from the permission matrix
nodes.rationale: The CSV form of permission-matrix §5 and §6 drives tests asserting allowed and denied actions, including URL and identifier tampering; policy drift fails the build.

nodes.label: Key flow 7.1: subscription purchase and activation
Idempotent payment webhook activation on provider_ref
nodes.rationale: Now an explicit AMPM requirement; the worker verifies the signature and idempotency before marking the payment and subscription active.

nodes.label: Key flow 7.2: RSVP submission through a family-group token
Key flow 7.3: approval of a vendor proposal version
Key flow 7.5: daily hotel freshness job
nodes.rationale: Verifications older than hotel_verification_max_age_days and dependent rate cards become stale, the search view is rebuilt and the Hotel team is notified; stale rates are never presented as confirmed.

nodes.label: Data layer (§8)
UUID v7 primary keys and indexing conventions
Prisma soft-delete client extension
nodes.rationale: Adds deleted_at IS NULL to every read and converts deletes to updates; retention jobs are the only code path that deletes rows.

nodes.label: Maintained hotel search view (tsvector and trigram index)
Demo isolation by is_demo scoping and nightly seed restore
Expand-and-contract migrations
nodes.rationale: No destructive migration ships with the code that depends on it; a release is reversible by redeploying the previous image.

Integration plan (§10): one adapter per provider
nodes.rationale: Each row lists the minimum data crossing the boundary and the onboarding lead time AMPM must start early.

nodes.label: Integration rules
nodes.rationale: Credentials in Secrets Manager only; every webhook verifies the signature, records the raw event and runs an idempotent job; sandbox mode for development and staging; a contract test per adapter in CI.

Integration: Amazon SES email
Integration: WhatsApp Business Platform via a provider
nodes.rationale: Opt-in required; template rejection falls back to SMS or email; Meta verification and template approval take 2 to 6 weeks (RK-4).

nodes.label: Integration: Indian SMS provider with DLT registration
nodes.rationale: SMS DLT registration becomes a launch dependency because OTP depends on it.

Integration: ICS calendar feed (Google Calendar sync later)
Integration: accounting export (CSV, Tally XML if used)
Integration: external hotel systems (none in v1, GP-39)
Integration: privacy-respecting website analytics
Security and privacy controls by layer (§11)
Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 controls
nodes.rationale: Consent at enquiry and RSVP, purpose limitation through field classes, data principal requests via support tooling with SA action and audit, retention jobs, breach runbook, grievance contact.

nodes.label: Identity document controls
nodes.rationale: Never Aadhaar; minimum fields; restricted bucket; automatic deletion after checkout plus 30 days; every read audited.

nodes.label: File handling controls
nodes.rationale: Type detection by content, size limits, antivirus scan in the worker before download, metadata stripping, private buckets, 15-minute signed URLs.

nodes.label: Environments: development, staging, production
nodes.rationale: Staging uses synthetic and anonymised data, never real guest data.

nodes.label: Delivery: trunk-based development, staging auto-deploy, tagged production releases
Deployment freeze while any project is live
nodes.rationale: Hotfixes only, with the project lead informed (T-14).

nodes.label: Wedding-day monitoring mode and on-call
nodes.rationale: While a project is live, alert thresholds tighten and the on-call engineer is named to the project lead.

Architecture risks and mitigations (§14)
Offline sync conflict handling
nodes.rationale: Local SQLite store, a change queue replayed with original timestamps, server wins on status transitions, a conflict log for everything else reviewed by the project lead, encryption at rest and wipe on sign-out.
